commenti.body: I don’t think it would work as well tbh. Gillis is a cocky asshole, which Holden does perfectly. Clift can do confident well (RED RIVER) but he’s too damn likable. And Clift’s other mode of acting is too neurotic for the role. Don’t think he’d be bad per se, he’s Montgomery Clift after all, but Holden works so well for the character

I recently made a post on here about Montgomery Clift and I have to say I agreed with everything you wrote. Clift was a unique actor that was extremely thorough when it came to his acting performances and he brought a depth and vulnerability to his roles that no other actor could at the time. Clift was also in his 20's so he was closer age wise to the character and until he had car accident and addictions took their toll he could believable play younger than his age. Holden is good, but I feel Clift could have been great and elevated everything with his performance.

I wouldn't call Gillis a "cocky asshole"; he's a droll, sarcastic opportunist, but he's a more layered character than that. 

Clift proved he could do villainous in *The Heiress* and "morally questionable" in *A Place in the Sun* and *Terminal Station*...no reason to think he couldn't do that here. 

He's upstanding and wholesome in *The Search*, but I think we would have seen a lot of that wisecracking, carefree aspect of that character in his interpretation of Gillis.

To repeat, I like Holden quite a bit, but I don't think he's in Clift's league as an actor; very few, if any, are. Pre-accident Clift was a special, one-of-a-kind actor, and you don't get more immersive than a performance where he's firing on all cylinders. 

His bosom pal Liz Taylor said that he would have been the biggest movie star ever had he simply made more movies, and there's a lot of truth to that, both when considering his extremely persnickety attitude towards scripts and his unfortunate early death.

He wasted so much of his prime years doing nothing, and finally when he decided to go back to work, it was for a giant flop that irrevocably changed his life for the worse. 

With the exception of *Rope* (how fascinating it would have been to see him and Hitch's other original choice, Grant together), I'm glad that the casting turned out the way it did for the other films. But *Sunset Blvd.* was the one he needed to make, and it hurts the most because it was external circumstances that forced him to bow out, as opposed to his artistic integrity.

> Holden is good, but I feel Clift could have been great and elevated everything with his performance.

I can’t see him playing the cocky asshole and narrator as well as William

> Clift deliver deadpan narration as perfectly as Holden does, which helps launch Sunset Blvd. into another stratosphere.

Yeah no one could have narrated this better than Holden
Cribbing "cocky asshole" does not mean you know the character. Quite the opposite...

Oh don't get me wrong I'm not knocking Holden or saying he was bad by any means. I actually do like him as an actor and feel he was good in Sunset Blvd. I even liked Alan Ladd a lot in Shane (another part Clift turned down). I think you articulated much better what I was trying to say which is that as good as Holden and Ladd were in Sunset Boulevard and Shane I feel Clift would have brought many nuances and depth to the roles in a way they couldn't. Sunset Boulevard would have been just as iconic with Clift in the main role. 

  
Also another criticism I hear is that Clift wouldn't have pulled off the cynical nararration. I disagree. I listened to a recording of The Glass Menagerie he did the year before died and while it was obvious from his voice he was in very bad shape he still managed to be very good and I have no doubt he would have worked out his narration for SB. Before his car accident and addictions took over Clift was at the top of his game.
Nah Ladd made Shane iconic Clift wouldn’t have been as believable in those fight scenes as Ladd was.

I actually do thank you very much Joe Gillis is a witty, Down on His Luck, and his career and ambitions have stalled and he has nothing left to do but stumble until he lucks into meeting Norma Desmond
Being witty and down on one's luck does not an asshole make, but there's point in addressing this further.
Clift couldn’t the anger and the inner struggle that Holden delivered in his performance. He was cheated out of an Oscar for this role

The rowboat scene in *A Place in the Sun* is the best-acted "inner turmoil" moment in movie history and nobody underplayed better than Monty.

I suggest familiarizing yourself with his movies before commenting on him.
I have seen his movies and my point still stands

An inability to convey tumult and overdoing it are simply not accusations any knowledgeable cineaste would make against Montgomery Clift. 

You get a participation ribbon though, thanks for your, erm, "contributions" to this discussion!
